phases.name: Pure decision logic: watchdog, translator, confirmation gate

steps.name: Run Watchdog stale-wave detection and wave-progress event derivation
steps.criteria: collectStaleWaves returns HALTED transitions for waves silent past the configured idle threshold and never for actively-producing waves, satisfying AC5's no-progress halt guarantee (scenario 7); deriveWaveProgressEvents derives nwave.run.wave_started/wave_completed/wave_failed domain events purely from process.started/output/exited events, never by parsing agent stdout, satisfying AC4 (scenario 8); Both functions are pure: same input state always yields the same output, no fetch/apiFetch/child_process import, verified by dependency-cruiser's no-nwave-invocation-pure-logic-io rule
steps.scenario_name: A wave that produces no output for longer than the configured threshold is halted with a clear 'no progress' signal; A run's wave-progress signal is derived from process lifecycle events, not from parsing agent output
steps.implementation_notes: Simplest pure functions first, no I/O, mirrors intent-watchdog.ts's ingestIntentEvents/collectDueIntentTimeouts pair exactly. Quality gate: unit-testable with synthetic event batches, no real process/HTTP/DB needed.

steps.name: Confirmation Gate: pure confirm/correct evaluation
steps.criteria: evaluateConfirmationResponse returns a CONFIRMED result only for an explicit affirmative submitter reply, never inferring confirmation from silence or an unrelated message (AC2); evaluateConfirmationResponse returns a CORRECTION result that re-requests a new restatement and explicitly withholds run start for a corrective reply (AC3, scenario 2); The evaluator is a pure function of the channel event and current gate state, taking no dependency on shell_start, HTTP, or the database
steps.scenario_name: Carlos corrects a misunderstood restatement and the run does not start until re-confirmed
steps.implementation_notes: Second-simplest pure function per acceptance-review.md's recommended order. Quality gate: dependency-cruiser rule confirms no I/O import; unit-testable with a synthetic channel event stream.

steps.name: Walking skeleton: restatement, confirmed-run trigger, HTTP repository
steps.criteria: composeRestatement generates and posts a plain-language restatement of a classified ticket's intent to its channel before any run exists, using a fake GenerateFn (AC1, scenario 14); triggerRunForConfirmedIntent calls RunRepositoryPort.createRun to assign a stable run id before spawning the first wave process via shell_start, then confirms and starts the run (AC2, AC4, scenario 1 WS); HttpRunRepository implements createRun/confirmRun/recordWaveStarted against real POST /api/nwave-runs, .../confirm, .../waves routes backed by the new nwave_runs/nwave_run_waves tables; The assigned run id is echoed unchanged in the run's confirm response and its first wave record, proving referential stability from the first wave transition onward (AC4, scenario 4); Deleting the real shell_start spawn, SQLite, or HTTP app would fail this walking skeleton immediately (Dimension 9d boundary proof)
steps.scenario_name: The system composes a plain-language restatement of the ticket's intent before any run starts; Maria confirms the system's understood intent and an nWave implementation run starts, identified by a stable run id; The run id remains stable and is referenced by every wave transition for the life of the run
steps.implementation_notes: Highest-value step: wires the real HTTP/SQLite/subprocess path (Strategy B per DWD-01) once the pure pieces from phase 01 are solid. Only the Restatement Composer's LLM generate() call is faked. Quality gate: nwave_run_waves.run_id is never processId (one-to-many); migration 028 adds nwave_runs/nwave_run_waves without touching the sibling track's nwave_run_stuck_flags table.

steps.name: Wave chaining and HTTP-driven run inspection/halt/idempotency
steps.criteria: advanceToNextWave chains DISCUSS, DESIGN, DISTILL, DELIVER strictly in order on each wave's clean exit, marking the run COMPLETED once DELIVER exits cleanly (AC4, AC5, scenario 12); GET /api/nwave-runs/:id returns the run's current status and full wave history through the real Hono app, backed by HttpRunRepository (AC4, scenario 5); POST /api/nwave-runs/:id/halt stops the active wave process and marks the run HALTED, and no further wave starts after halting (AC5, scenario 9); A redelivered wave-completion notification for an already-recorded wave is a no-op and never advances the run a second time (AC5 at-least-once idempotency, scenario 10)
steps.scenario_name: Wave chaining follows DISCUSS, DESIGN, DISTILL, DELIVER in order, and the run completes once DELIVER exits cleanly; A run's current status and wave history are observable through the run detail view; A stalled run can be halted through the run's halt action, and no further waves proceed after halting; A redelivered wave-completion notification does not advance the run a second time
steps.implementation_notes: Builds outward from the walking skeleton per ADR-0002's one-process-per-wave chaining. Idempotency guard (scenario 10) must key off the wave's own recorded status, not a separate dedup table, matching the platform's existing at-least-once event semantics. This track's 6 routes only; the file's other 7 handlers belong to multi-source-ingestion-governance.

phases.name: Failure hardening and external CLI contract

steps.name: Start-failure, non-zero exit, and access-control safety
steps.criteria: A shell_start spawn failure at run creation marks the run START_FAILED, references the already-assigned run id, and never emits a wave-progress event implying work is underway (AC5, scenario 3); A wave process exiting non-zero marks that wave and the run FAILED and halts the chain, so the next wave never starts (AC5, scenario 6); No nwave_runs row exists and no run is ever shown as in progress until the submitter's confirmation is observed by the Confirmation Gate (AC2, scenario 11); Every /api/nwave-runs* route rejects a request carrying no authenticated session with 401 before touching run state (implicit access control, scenario 13)
steps.scenario_name: Maria is told clearly a run could not start when the execution environment is unavailable, never shown false progress; A wave that exits with a non-zero code fails the run and halts the chain without starting the next wave; Before any confirmation is observed, no run is ever created or shown as in progress; Someone with no authenticated session cannot halt or inspect an implementation run
steps.implementation_notes: Consolidates the top-priority quality attribute (reliability/fault tolerance, brief.md line 33): a failed trigger is never silently 'in progress'. The access-control scenario is expected to be largely a regression check against the existing global /api/* auth gate (apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts), same pattern the sibling track documented for its own access-control scenario.

steps.name: nWave CLI headless invocation contract (CI-only, gated)
steps.criteria: A fixed-input/fixed-expected-shape smoke test invokes the real headless nWave CLI command and asserts its flags/exit-code/output-shape contract, skipped locally without the gating fixture (brief.md's recommendation, scenario 15); This test is excluded from local development per brief.md's own scope note and runs only in the CI acceptance stage once the fixture is provisioned
steps.scenario_name: The nWave CLI headless invocation contract remains stable (skipped without fixture)
steps.implementation_notes: Smallest step, deliberately last: covers brief.md's own-named single highest-risk boundary (the nWave CLI invocation surface) via a gated @requires_external contract test, not Pact (CLI, not a REST/GraphQL API). Contract tests recommended for the nWave CLI invocation surface in the CI acceptance stage per platform-architect handoff.

validation.findings_summary: All gates passed: 15/15 scenarios covered, max step size 4/8, walking skeleton in Phase 2 (early, not deferred). No blockers. Dependency graph enables parallelism. Quality criteria evidence-based.
